{{technical|date=May 2025}}
}}The '''Stokes operator''', named after [[George Gabriel Stokes]], is an unbounded [[linear operator]] used in the theory of [[partial differential equation]]s, specifically in the fields of [[fluid dynamics]] and [[electromagnetics]].

==Definition==

If we define <math>P_\sigma</math> as the [[Leray projection]] onto [[divergence]] free [[vector field]]s, then the Stokes Operator <math>A</math> is defined by

:<math>A:=-P_\sigma\Delta,</math>

where <math>\Delta\equiv\nabla^2</math> is the [[Laplacian]].  Since <math>A</math> is unbounded, we must also give its domain of definition, which is defined as <math>\mathcal{D}(A)=H^2\cap V</math>, where <math>V=\{\vec{u}\in (H^1_0(\Omega))^n|\operatorname{div}\,\vec{u}=0\}</math>.  Here, <math>\Omega</math> is a bounded open set in <math>\mathbb{R}^n</math> (usually ''n''&nbsp;=&nbsp;2 or 3), <math>H^2(\Omega)</math> and <math>H^1_0(\Omega)</math> are the standard [[Sobolev spaces]], and the divergence of <math>\vec{u}</math> is taken in the [[Distribution (mathematics)|distribution]] sense.

==Properties==

For a given domain <math>\Omega</math> which is open, bounded, and has <math>C^2</math> boundary, the Stokes operator <math>A</math> is a [[self-adjoint]] [[Positive-definite operator|positive-definite]] operator with respect to the <math>L^2</math> inner product.  It has an orthonormal basis of eigenfunctions <math>\{w_k\}_{k=1}^\infty</math> corresponding to eigenvalues <math>\{\lambda_k\}_{k=1}^\infty</math> which satisfy

:<math>0<\lambda_1<\lambda_2\leq\lambda_3\cdots\leq\lambda_k\leq\cdots</math>

and <math>\lambda_k\rightarrow\infty</math> as <math>k\rightarrow\infty</math>.  Note that the smallest eigenvalue is unique and non-zero.  These properties allow one to define powers of the Stokes operator.  Let <math>\alpha>0</math> be a real number.  We define <math>A^\alpha</math> by its action on <math>\vec{u}\in \mathcal{D}(A)</math>:

:<math>A^\alpha \vec{u}=\sum_{k=1}^\infty \lambda_k^{\alpha} u_k\vec{w_k}</math>

where <math>u_k:=(\vec{u},\vec{w_k})</math> and <math>(\cdot,\cdot)</math> is the <math>L^2(\Omega)</math> inner product.

The inverse <math>A^{-1}</math> of the Stokes operator is a bounded, compact, self-adjoint operator in the space <math>H:=\{\vec{u}\in (L^2(\Omega))^n| \operatorname{div}\,\vec{u}=0 \text{ and }\gamma(\vec{u})=0\}</math>, where <math>\gamma</math> is the [[Trace_operator#Generalized_normal_trace|trace operator]].  Furthermore, <math>A^{-1}:H\rightarrow V</math> is injective.
